newsitem.title: ISRAEL: FOREIGN MEDIA URGE PLO TO FREE PALESTINIAN NEWSMAN.
newsitem.headline: FOREIGN MEDIA URGE PLO TO FREE PALESTINIAN NEWSMAN.

text.p: The Foreign Press Association representing media in Israel and the Palestinian Authority urged the authority on Thursday to free Palestinian journalist Daoud Kuttab promptly.
"The FPA urges prompt action to release journalist Daoud Kuttab. As far as we understand, no charges have been brought against him," it said in a statement.

"It is widely understood that he was detained for broadcasting stories from the Palestinian Legislative Council. If true, such action would be a serious and grave restraint on free expression, inconsistent with free journalism."
A French media rights group, Reporters sans Frontieres (Reporters without Borders), said in Paris that it had asked Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to free Kuttab.
On Wednesday, Speaker of the Palestinian Legislative Council Ahmed Korei announced to legislators Kuttab's detention by police and said the council would demand an explanation.

Kuttab's brother told Reuters on Wednesday that Kuttab was summoned to Ramallah by Palestinian police. The journalist, who lives in East Jerusalem, went to the Ramallah self-rule enclave in the West Bank and was detained.

The brother said the detention was apparently related to a dispute between Kuttab, who has a private contract to carry live broadcasts of Palestinian Legislative Council sessions, and Palestinian state-run television.

"He has been running into problems with jamming of their broadcast by the Palestinian authorities, by Palestinian television, in order to block council sessions critical of the Palestinian Authority," the brother, Jonathan Kuttab, said.
"There are some people within the executive branch who do not feel comfortable with that level of openness or criticism."
Kuttab is dean of the Modern Communications Centre at al-Quds University.

He was awarded the International Press Freedom Award last year by the New York-based Committee to Protect Journalists for his work challenging censorship practices of both Israeli and Palestinian authorities.
